ns2:section.sectionText: Kierkegaard & Company: Existentialism, Pietism & the Discovery of Self (meets with CWL 441 and PHIL 444) Graduate section Soren Kierkegaard is an early author and philosopher who wrestled with the concept of the individual self and even championed subjective experience as a counterbalance to objective rationalism. These concepts were born in response to two currents that were developing in the 19th century, one of them philosophical, Existentialism, and the other one religious, Pietism. Students in this seminar-style course will gain extensive familiarity with all the major works of Kierkegaard, as well as mastery of foundational concepts presented in them. Kierkegaard will be evaluated within his particular Nordic literary context, through critical analysis of related novels, plays and films by Andersen, Ibsen, Bremer, Strindberg, Lagerlof, Blixen, and Bergman (all readings will be in English translation).
